audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph postexilic Jerusalem inhabitants, priests, Levites, gatekeepers, service workers, and repeated Saul genealogy, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for exile blame, return and resettlement, temple servants/Nethinim, tribal inclusion, priestly and Levitical hierarchy, gatekeeping and treasury work, food and craft labor, day-and-night service, hereditary office, and repetition of Saul's line.

verses.restored: All Israel was enrolled by genealogy; look, they were written in scroll of kings of Israel. Judah was carried away to Babylon for unfaithfulness, in narrator's theology.
First inhabitants who lived again in their possessions and cities were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
In Jerusalem lived some from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh:
Uthai son of Ammihud son of Omri son of Imri son of Bani, from descendants of Perez son of Judah.
From Shilonites: Asaiah firstborn and his sons.
From sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their relatives—six hundred ninety.
From sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam son of Hodaviah son of Hassenuah,
Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi son of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah son of Reuel son of Ibnijah.
Their relatives according to generations were nine hundred fifty-six. All these were heads of ancestral houses.
From priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
Azariah son of Hilkiah son of Meshullam son of Zadok son of Meraioth son of Ahitub, ruler/official of house of Divine,
Adaiah son of Jeroham son of Pashhur son of Malchijah, and Maasai son of Adiel son of Jahzerah son of Meshullam son of Meshillemith son of Immer.
Their relatives, heads of ancestral houses, were one thousand seven hundred sixty, capable people for work of service of house of Divine.
From Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub son of Azrikam son of Hashabiah, from descendants of Merari;
Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica son of Zichri son of Asaph;
Obadiah son of Shemaiah son of Galal son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah son of Asa son of Elkanah, who lived in villages of Netophathites.
Gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives; Shallum was chief.
Until then he served at king's gate eastward. They were gatekeepers in camps/divisions of Levites.

Shallum son of Kore son of Ebiasaph son of Korah and relatives of his ancestral house, Korahites, were over service work, guarding thresholds of tent; their ancestors had guarded entrance of camp of YHWH.
Phinehas son of Eleazar had been leader over them in past, and YHWH was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at entrance of tent of meeting.
All chosen as gatekeepers at thresholds were two hundred twelve. They were enrolled by genealogy in villages; David and Samuel the seer established them in trusted office.
They and their descendants had oversight of gates of house of YHWH, the tent-house, by watches.
Gatekeepers were on four sides: east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives in villages came at intervals for seven days to serve with them.
Four chief gatekeepers, Levites, were in trusted office over chambers and treasuries of house of Divine.
They lodged around house of Divine because watch was upon them, and opening it morning by morning was their responsibility.
Some were responsible for vessels of service, bringing them in and out by count.
Some were appointed over furniture, all sanctuary vessels, fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
Some sons of priests compounded ointment of spices.
Mattithiah, a Levite, firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had trusted responsibility over things baked in pans.
Some of their Kohathite relatives were over bread of presence, preparing it Sabbath by Sabbath.
These were singers, heads of Levite ancestral houses, living in chambers and free from other duties, because they were engaged in work day and night.
These were heads of Levite ancestral houses throughout generations; they lived in Jerusalem.
At Gibeon lived Jeiel father/founder of Gibeon; name of his wife was Maacah.
His firstborn Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth fathered Shimeam. They also lived opposite relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner fathered Kish; Kish fathered Saul; Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
Son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; Merib-baal fathered Micah.
Sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jarah; Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri fathered Moza.
Moza fathered Binea; Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were sons of Azel.

translation_notes: The opening attributes exile to unfaithfulness, but Babylonian deportation remains imperial violence suffered by civilians, workers, children, and later generations.
Returnees are not the only legitimate inhabitants of the land; postexilic resettlement must not erase people who remained or other communities living there.
Nethinim/temple servants may reflect subordinated or inherited service status. Sacred service must not conceal coerced labor or caste.
Ephraim and Manasseh are represented in Jerusalem, complicating simplistic claims that northern Israel disappeared completely.
Gatekeepers, inventory workers, cooks, spice compounders, bakers, singers, and night workers are skilled religious labor, not background help.
Hereditary trusted office does not guarantee trustworthiness or remove accountability and safeguarding requirements.
Day-and-night service should not justify exploitative schedules, sleep deprivation, or unpaid religious labor.
The repeated Saul genealogy preserves Esh-baal and Merib-baal name forms without shame; disability stigma and polemical renaming are rejected.
Chronicles and Nehemiah contain differing names and counts for postexilic residents and require source audit.
safety_note: Do not blame exiles for empire, erase people who remained in the land, defend hereditary temple servitude, exploit religious workers, or treat genealogical enrollment as citizenship purity. Sacred institutions owe safety, rest, compensation, and dignity to every worker.
